source.title: DoWG Unleashed: An Efficient Universal Parameter-Free Gradient Descent Method
source.authors: Ahmed Khaled; Konstantin Mishchenko; Chi Jin

record.file_problem: Full paper and supplementary material are present. The extracted text has some flattened equations and plots, but the relevant experimental discussion is readable.
record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates a new adaptive optimizer on image classifiers and reports held-out performance alongside training behavior, extending optimizer comparisons to DoWG. It does not compare DoWG with SGD.
record.gate_note: The CIFAR-10 experiments compare DoWG, DoG, L-DoG, tuned AdaGrad-norm, and Adam. The paper reports training loss and test accuracy, but gives no numeric values in the text. Its optimizer comparison is relevant to generalization, but does not test V4's adaptive-method-versus-SGD comparison.
record.test_reason: The study compares DoWG with other adaptive optimizers on CIFAR-10, without an SGD or momentum-SGD comparator. These results do not test V4's optimizer comparison or any other listed version. Its convergence and edge-of-stability results also do not measure the generalization relationship in V7.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the experimental discussion: DoWG uses larger step sizes, is less stable on ResNet-50, and performs differently against Adam depending on iterate averaging. The paper's main conclusion is that DoWG is a parameter-free, universal optimizer with convex convergence guarantees and competitive practical performance.
record.recipe_differences: The paper proposes and evaluates DoWG, a parameter-free optimizer. It compares optimizers on CIFAR-10 rather than testing the catalog's original interventions or comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports a difference between DoWG's last and polynomially averaged iterates; it also notes that DoWG is less stable on ResNet-50.

fits_no_version.finding: On CIFAR-10 with VGG11 and ResNet-50, the authors report worse test accuracy for DoWG's last iterate than Adam, while polynomially averaged DoWG often performs better.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: DoWG's held-out performance relative to Adam depends on whether the last or polynomially averaged iterate is evaluated.

record.problems: The text gives no numeric test-accuracy values or uncertainty estimates for the CIFAR-10 comparisons. The prose does not separate the stated DoWG-versus-Adam result by architecture; results are averaged over 8 random seeds.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant results were reported in the text. Figure 4 plots training loss, test accuracy, and step sizes, but the text does not give separate numerical outcomes for each plotted curve.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and the corresponding natural-label and random-label held-out accuracy.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD or momentum SGD, tuning-dependent differences, and the specified recovery interventions.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and changes that recover performance.
Dropout's effect on held-out error across training regimes.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance versus generalization gaps and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus removing equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Figure 4's caption calls the middle panels training loss, while their extracted axis labels say training accuracy. Neither interpretation supplies a missing comparison testing a listed version.

versions.untested_parts: Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
The experiments do not compare adaptive methods with SGD or momentum SGD; no language benchmarks or broader tuning comparison are reported.
No sharpness or other generalization measure is compared with the train–test gap.

rows.subject: VGG11 and ResNet-50 (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Train on CIFAR-10 with DoWG's last iterate and compare test accuracy with Adam.
rows.baseline: Adam with cosine annealing and standard step size 10−3
rows.value: DoWG last iterate gives worse test accuracy than Adam
rows.note: The text states this comparison without separating VGG11 from ResNet-50; aggregate result across the two tested architectures.
rows.check: This is the proposed method's performance against Adam, outside all listed versions; 'reversed' is therefore inapplicable. The qualitative value matches Section 4, but the subject combines two architectures rather than recording separate model results.

rows.subject: VGG11 and ResNet-50 (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Train on CIFAR-10 with DoWG's polynomially averaged iterate and compare test accuracy with Adam.
rows.baseline: Adam with cosine annealing and standard step size 10−3
rows.value: The average iterate of DoWG often performs better
rows.note: The text does not specify which architecture or conditions account for 'often'; aggregate statement across the experiments.
rows.check: This is the proposed method's performance against Adam, outside all listed versions; 'partial' is therefore inapplicable. Section 4 supports the qualitative statement but does not identify which architecture or epochs account for the reported advantage.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
